design:
D1 Owner. A new module, hub/hub/builds.py, owns the build record and the level policy: LEVELS, who may approve at a level, the evidence rule a level implies, and allows_automatic_override(level). It decides nothing about moves: slice B's decide_move (task_transition_service.py:467) stays the one decision and reads the level as an input, and requirement_gate keeps the evidence decision, reading builds' rule where it reads document rigor today (requirement_gate.py:1217-1228). Fast maps to sketch's rule, Reviewed to contract's (reported, never refused), Gated to gate's. A task with no build keeps its document's rigor, so nothing built before this change, and no task created outside a build, behaves differently.

D2 Record and engine. The build row holds the settings; the flow and lead drivers each own one Loop, the row the scheduler already fires, advances after commit (flow_advance.py:39, called from task_transition_service.py:979) and stops, so no second scheduling mechanism appears. The hand driver owns no loop. One running build per document: a partial unique index on (document_id) where state is running, the precedent ux_loops_spec_document_live (models.py:2001-2007). A Loop created before this change has no build and runs as today. Slice C's Build route and 'Approve and build' create the build; the recommended build slice C records gains these settings, and C's delivery mode flow/none reads as driver flow/hand.

D3 People. builders narrows _agents_a_loop_may_staff (scheduler.py:1696) and the job's default agent is the first builder; reviewers narrows rung 2 of resolve_reviewer (scheduler.py:1888). A task's declared reviewer (rung 1) and declared builder win over the pools. The declared builder becomes the assignee at build start, not at approval (slice C: approval is a plan): the flow already resumes an assigned task only on its assignee (scheduler.py:2375-2377), which is the mechanism F1046 points at. Empty lists mean today's behaviour.

D4 Levels. Fast adds one edge, completed -> approved, which decide_move allows only at Fast and only to the task's builder, the build's lead and the operator; in a flow-driven Fast build no review is staged, and the flow approves (origin job, as the operator's job authority, task_transition_service.py:827-830) once the task's check run passes, asked from project_checks._announce_finished (project_checks.py:854) through flow_advance. The edge, rather than letting the builder take its own task into review, keeps 'an author holds its task under review' false at every level (slice B's _guard_reviewer_is_not_the_author). Reviewed and Gated keep slice B's anyone-but-the-builder rule. Close-as-built (already_built.py:138) takes a level; at Fast its evidence is recorded accepted and the tasks approved at once (slice B's resolved question). tasks.level is written at build start and task_transitions.level on every move of a task in a build.

D5 Checks at every level. Approval still calls evaluate_approval with start_checks (task_transition_service.py:918-929) whatever the level, and slice L's ordering applies unchanged. Slice M's automatic override asks builds.allows_automatic_override: true at Fast and Reviewed (subject to M's project setting), false at Gated. The operator picks Gated to judge every landing; at Gated, M's fix task still heads the flow and the approval lands when its checks pass.

D6 Lead. A lead-driven build's firing does not select work: it queues one brief to the lead's build conversation, listing open tasks, holders, free builders, level, spend and window, unless the previous brief is still unread. hand_out_task assigns and queues the chosen agent's turn bound to the task the way the operator's trigger does (task_id / review_task_id, agent_trigger.py:487-501), and refuses any caller that is not the lead of the task's running build and any agent outside the build's pools. The lead approves through update_task under D4's rules. It gets no general assignee power (slice B's non-goal stands).

D7 Budget and window. Spend is the sum of turn_usage.api_equivalent_usd_micros over runs bound to the build's tasks and runs in the lead's build conversation; a turn with no figure counts zero and the build view counts it as unpriced. USD rather than tokens because that is the unit the operator measured the nights in, and it is recorded on 428 of 436 turns on :8000. Each flow or lead firing asks builds.may_hand_out first; at the cap the loop stops with stop_reason naming spend and cap, a stall-free operator notification is sent, and Raise cap / a later window restarts the loop. Running turns are never stopped.

D8 Landing. main merges as today. nowhere makes _integrate_task (task_transition_service.py:1276) record a skip with the reason before any git call. A named branch is not offered (non-goals).

Hazard (Tier 2). Migration: a builds table; tasks.build_id (indexed, no foreign key, the precedent Task.loop_id, models.py:760-764) and tasks.level; task_transitions.level. No backfill: null means built outside a build and governed as today. Rollback: downgrade drops the index, the three columns and the table; nothing existing is rewritten. Live data on :8000 (read-only, 2026-10-27): 0 open spec tasks, 1 live flow loop, which has no build and keeps running as today. Back up :8000 with the sqlite backup API before its first start on this code. Cross-cutting: decide_move and requirement_gate are consulted by every path that moves or approves a task; slice B's invariant test, extended over levels and the lead, is what stops a level from adding a dead end.

Split. Amendments, retiring rigor, the main watch and the next-slice offer are slice D2 (split accepted 2026-10-27).

problem:
Every spec is built with the same ceremony whatever its risk, and nobody chooses who builds it.
- 2026-10-26/27, slice B's flow (operator's :8000): T3 was built by the Architect (Opus, 41 min, ~$6) because a flow hands fresh work to whichever agent is free: `decide_firing` takes the first free agent (hub/hub/scheduler.py:2444-2478) from `_agents_a_loop_may_staff` (scheduler.py:1696-1720), which knows no list of builders. The night cost ~$44 API-equivalent over 6 h 47 min, $11.2 of it Opus QA, and three reviews found only what the failing check had already found.
- 2026-10-25 (F1046, branch agentweave/Architect, scripts/drive/FINDINGS.md:40509): a spec task can name its reviewer but not who builds it (`spec_payload.Task`, hub/hub/spec_payload.py:136-167); approval creates every task with `assignee=None` (hub/hub/spec_tasks.py:416), so routing a task to the stronger model means setting assignees by hand after approval.
- The rule that the builder never approves is unconditional (`_guard_author_is_not_reviewer`, hub/hub/task_transition_service.py:504-552), so there is no way to say 'this one is low risk, let the builder land it'.
- How strictly evidence is enforced is a property of the document (`SpecDocument.rigor`, hub/hub/db/models.py:2400-2405, read by requirement_gate.py:1217-1228), not of how it is built; on :8000 every one of 180 documents is `sketch` (read-only query, 2026-10-27).
- Nothing records how a spec was built: approval creates one flow from `delivery` (hub/hub/api/v1/spec.py:3490-3620) with an agent, a cron and a stop condition, and `Loop` has no builders, reviewers, budget or level (models.py:1893-2008). The only cost limit is the project-wide token budget (models.py:84, usage_accounting.py:508-535), so a build cannot be capped.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-10-26: how a spec is built is chosen when building starts, not inside the spec; the record is what slices F and G read.
requirements.statement: Starting a build of an approved document records a build with its driver (flow, lead or hand), level (fast, reviewed or gated), builders, reviewer pool, lead, budget cap, window and landing, readable afterwards from the document; Build and 'Approve and build' open with the recommended build filled in; a second build of the same document is refused while one is running, naming it.

requirements.rationale: 'Every task records the level it was built under' (roadmap); a null level keeps every flow and task created before this change behaving as it does now.
requirements.statement: Every task a build covers records that build and its level when the build starts (or when it joins a running build), and every transition of that task records the level that governed it; a task outside any build records none and is governed exactly as today.

requirements.rationale: F1046. Kept rather than refused for the reason `reviewer` is (spec_payload.py:164-167): an author cannot know which agents the running machine has. Applied at build start, not approval, because slice C makes approval a plan.
requirements.statement: A spec task may declare a builder by agent name; when a build starts, a declared builder that is an open agent becomes the task's assignee unless the operator changed it in the Build dialog, and one that is not is kept on the task, reported in the start's response, and the task left for the driver to hand out.

requirements.rationale: 2026-10-27: T3 went to the Architect (Opus) only because it was free.
requirements.statement: A flow-driven build hands fresh work only to its builders and staffs reviews only from its reviewer pool (each list, when empty, meaning any free agent as today); a task's own declared builder or reviewer still takes precedence; no other agent is given a turn on the build's tasks.

requirements.rationale: The lead exercises the judgement the 2026-10-25 retrospective found missing in the middle; its authority is scoped to one build (roadmap non-goal: no project-wide god agent).
requirements.statement: A lead-driven build gives its lead a turn when it starts and whenever one of its tasks is completed, sent back, approved or rejected, without stacking a second brief on an unread one; the lead hands a task to one of the build's builders, or a review to one of its reviewer pool, with a tool answered only for the lead of that task's running build; a hand-driven build starts no turn at all.

requirements.rationale: Slice B's non-goal names Fast as where author-may-not-approve becomes a choice; slice B's resolved question says already-built tasks close at once at Fast.
requirements.statement: At Fast, a completed task is approved without a reviewer turn: by its builder or its build's lead directly from completed, or, in a flow-driven build, by the flow once the task's check run has passed; and closing a document's tasks as already built (slice B) at Fast approves them at once.

At Reviewed, any agent other than the task's builder (the lead included) or the operator approves it, and requirements the task serves that lack accepted evidence are reported in the approval's response, never refused.
At Gated, the builder cannot approve, and approval is refused until every requirement the task serves has evidence accepted, as a `gate`-rigor document's tasks are today.

requirements.rationale: Roadmap non-goal: at every level red checks mean no merge. Fast removes the reviewer, not the checks. Gated is chosen to judge every landing, so a Hub judgement that a failure is not the task's does not land it there.
requirements.statement: At every level, approval lands work only on passing project checks or an override: the operator's with a reason at any level, or slice M's automatic override at Fast and Reviewed only, never at Gated.

requirements.rationale: The night of 2026-10-26/27 cost ~$44 with nothing to stop it; turn_usage carries api_equivalent_usd_micros on 428 of 436 turns on :8000 (read-only query, 2026-10-27).
requirements.statement: A flow- or lead-driven build hands out no new turn before its window opens, after it closes, or once the API-equivalent cost of its runs reaches its cap; turns already running finish; reaching the cap stops the build with the spend and the cap in its reason and notifies the operator, and raising the cap or extending the window resumes it.

A build lands its approved work on the project's main branch as today, or nowhere: a task of a build that lands nowhere is approved with nothing merged and its integration record says the build lands nowhere.

requirements.rationale: Slice B's invariant, extended: levels and a lead are new inputs to its one decision, and must not add a dead end.
requirements.statement: For every level, every non-terminal status and every holder (none, the builder, another agent, the mender, the build's lead), at least one actor can move the task on with the tools it is offered, blocked excepted (its mover is the operator).

in_scope: A build record created by slice C's Build action (and 'Approve and build'), holding driver, level, builders, reviewer pool, lead, budget cap, window and landing; one running build per document
The flow driver drawing fresh work only from the build's builders and reviews only from its reviewer pool
The lead driver: a lead agent briefed when the build starts and when its work is handed on, handing tasks to builders and reviews to the pool with a tool scoped to its build
The hand driver: nothing is started; tasks wait on the board with their builders assigned
Fast, Reviewed and Gated as inputs to slice B's mover decision and to the evidence gate; slice B's close-as-built approving at once at Fast (B's open question)
A per-task builder in the spec payload (F1046) and the recommended build's new settings beside slice C's recommendation
Each task recording its build and level, and each transition the level that governed it
A budget cap in API-equivalent dollars and a window, both stopping new turns, never running ones
Landing on the project's main branch or nowhere
Which levels allow slice M's automatic check override
The Build dialog's settings and the build's state on today's spec header and task drawer
non_goals: Amendments after approval proposed by the author and the lead and accepted by the operator, retiring document rigor, raising main moving outside the Hub's integration, and offering the next slice's drafting when a build finishes: roadmap slice D2, spec/changes/amendments-main-watch-and-the-next-slice/
Retiring `SpecDocument.rigor`: a task in a build is governed by its level; a task outside any build keeps today's rigor behaviour until slice D2 retires the setting

Landing on a named branch other than the main branch: integration merges in the project's checkout and refuses one on another branch (task_integration.py:742-745); merging elsewhere belongs to slice E
The order of checks around completion and review: slice L, which applies unchanged at every level
Detecting a check failure that is not the task's and filing its fix task: slice M; this document only says at which levels its override may land work
The mender's waking rules: slice N
Per-level statistics: slice G reads what this records
A redesigned build view: slice F; this document extends today's header and drawer
Giving agents an assignee field on update_task: only the lead's scoped hand-out tool assigns, as slice B's non-goal keeps it
Killing a running turn when a budget or window ends

summary: Building an approved spec becomes a recorded build with settings the operator chooses when they press Build (slice C's action): a driver that hands out the work (the Hub's flow, a lead agent, or nobody: by hand), a gate level (Fast: the builder or the lead approves; Reviewed: anyone but the builder; Gated: as today, evidence accepted per requirement), the builders the work may go to, a reviewer pool, a lead, a budget cap, a window and where the work lands. A spec task may name its builder (F1046), and every task records the build and the level it was built under. Levels are new inputs to slice B's one mover decision and to the evidence gate, not new scattered checks; at every level red checks still mean no merge. Amendments after approval, raising main moving outside the Hub's integration, and offering the next slice's drafting are roadmap slice D2 (amendments-main-watch-and-the-next-slice), split off on 2026-10-27 because the whole slice did not fit four reviewable tasks.
